executive_summary: TechCorp's Information Security Policy demonstrates a good understanding of cryptographic standards, but there are significant deviations from the National Cryptographic Standards. The policy correctly implements AES for standard data encryption and utilizes Elliptic Curve Cryptography for key agreement in the Advanced zone. However, several violations were found, including the reuse of Initialization Vectors for stream ciphers and the use of insecure key lengths for RSA. To achieve full compliance, TechCorp must address these violations and implement the recommended changes.
compliant_areas: Utilization of AES for standard data encryption (Section 2.1.2 of the framework context)
Use of Elliptic Curve Cryptography for key agreement in the Advanced zone (Section 2.2 of the framework context)
Implementation of SHA-2 for digital signatures (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
violations: Reuse of Initialization Vectors for stream ciphers, which is prohibited by Section 2.1.1 of the framework context
Use of RSA with a 2048-bit key length, which is not accepted for the Advanced zone (Section 2.2 of the framework context)
Utilization of SOSEMANUK stream cipher with a 256-bit key for the Advanced zone, which is not accepted (Section 2.1.1 of the framework context)
Use of SHA-2 (SHA2-384) for digital signatures in the Advanced zone, which is not accepted (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
Use of SHA-2 (SHA2-512/256) for integrity in the Advanced zone, which is not accepted (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
Utilization of SHAKE128 with an output size of 128 bits, which does not meet the requirement of at least 256 bits (Section 2.3 of the framework context)
recommendations: Implement a secure random number generator to generate unique Initialization Vectors for each encryption operation
Upgrade RSA key length to at least 3072 bits for the Moderate zone and use a different algorithm for the Advanced zone
Replace SOSEMANUK stream cipher with a accepted algorithm, such as AES-CTR or Camellia-CTR, for the Advanced zone
Use SHA-3 (SHA3-512) for digital signatures and integrity in the Advanced zone
Increase the output size of SHAKE128 to at least 256 bits for lightweight hashing
